I think that's the most reasonable and practical thing to do. Please think about it, and I hope for an answer at the next Status Conference, which would be set within the next two months. So you have two months to think about that, two months to come up with an estimate of the time you need before you can be ready to start the trial. One last issue that I would wish to raise before we completely run out of time -- and I thank the interpreters for their patience and for their endurance, thank you, because they are working extra time, they were supposed to work for only one hour and a half, and we've been working for over two hours now, but we are reaching the end of the Status Conference, rest assured -- there is a motion that has been submitted by Mr. Kolundzija on March 17th. I think that the Prosecution has until the end of this month to answer to that motion. The motion is related to interference with witnesses. It is alleged that the Prosecution has tried to interfere with witnesses. This, of course, will be looked into by the Trial Chamber, the three Judges of the Trial Chamber. But I would like to turn to Mr. Kolundzija's Defence counsel. Is the Defence alleging that the Prosecution witnesses are, in fact, being interfered with? Are we talking about Prosecution witnesses here? Are these the witnesses that we're talking about at the very centre of the Defence motion? You have to stand up, sir, and could you please switch on your microphone. Microphone, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. AARON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour. The issue with that motion was interference with the witnesses by Bosnian authorities, not by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Aaron. So the Bosnian authorities are alleged to interfere with witnesses, so this has nothing to do with the Prosecution interfering with them. Do the Prosecution team members wish to say anything on this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're going to submit a written response to this motion which, I believe, is a motion that -- is a motion for discovery and uses examples of alleged torture as a reason for the remedies that are sought, and we will respond to that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Hollis. Unless either of the parties wishes to raise other issues, because Status Conferences are specifically designed for that, unless that is the case, I will go on to the last item on the agenda, i.e., the state of mind and the physical state of the accused. I now turn to the Defence. Mr. Petrovic, Mr. Vucicevic, is there anything you would like to say on this particular issue? Or is there any other issue that you would wish to raise, other than the question of the state of mind and the physical state of the accused? Is there something you would wish to raise on procedural matters, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Vucicevic, what about you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have anything to raise concerning the state of mind and treatment of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Vucicevic. Is there something else you would like to talk about from a procedural point of view, anything about the pre-trial proceedings, for example, that you would wish to discuss?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There was -- when you requested of the Office of the Prosecutor to submit all the witness statements, Madam Hollis indicated that there would be a synopsis on the background that is going to be attached to the witness statements. If any of the documentation that is going to be -- actually, any and all documentation that is going to be submitted to the Trial Chamber, we would like to receive the same copies so that we could be adequately prepared. Point number 1. Point number 2: In the mode of the presentation of evidence, Madam Hollis indicated that there is going to be a statement prepared to which a witness is going to ask to agree before presenting his evidence. I would deem that to be an infringement of the defendant's right to confront the accuser against him, because we will not be able to cross-examine those pieces of papers. If they are facts, the witnesses should testify. If not -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vucicevic, Ms. Hollis relies on legal procedures. The witnesses' statements are taken by the Prosecution. In themselves, they are not considered as evidence. They just make it possible for the Prosecution to prepare itself to examine the witness. So Ms. Hollis is not making up anything. Ms. Hollis, is there anything you would wish to discuss, from a procedural point of view, before I close this part of the Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and I don't want to try your patience, but I do need to clarify Mr. Vucicevic's understanding of what I attempted to say earlier. The Prosecution does not intend to submit witness statements, nor does it intend to submit a synopsis attached to these witness statements, unless something occurs during the trial that would lead us to submit them in some way as evidence. If we did so, of course the Defence would receive whatever we were to provide to the Trial Chamber as evidence. So his understanding of what I attempted to say earlier is incorrect, and I apologise if I was not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. So that would clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: This does clarify the point. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will now go into private session. Closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: adjourned at 5.05 p.m.
